artists.biography:
Big Big Train is an English progressive rock band that was founded in 1990. Based in Bournemouth, England, the band members are Nick D'Virgilio, Dave Gregory, David Longdon, Danny Manners, Andy Poole and Gregory Spawton.

Their first album, Goodbye To The Age of Steam was released in 1994 and was co-produced by Martin Orford of IQ. Age of Steam established the typical melancholy BBT sound influenced by progressive rock from the mid and early 1970s.

After two releases which featured more accessible music, BBT went back to their roots in 2004 and released a concept album called Gathering Speed. This album featured layers of 12-string guitar and mellotron and also hints at a growing post rock influence. Whilst arguably more derivative than some of their earlier releases, Gathering Speed was a very assured album and was critically well received.

With a new singer, Sean Filkins, and with Steve Hughes back on drums after stints with The Enid and Kino, BBT released their fifth studio album, The Difference Machine, in 2007. The album features performances from Nick D'Virgilio (Spock's Beard, Genesis, Tears for Fears); Dave Meros (Spock's Beard) and Pete Trewavas (Marillion, Transatlantic, Kino) In 2008 BBT released an updated version of their 1997 album, English Boy Wonders.

BBT released their sixth studio album, The Underfall Yard, on 15 December 2009. Steve Hughes and Sean Filkins left the band prior to the recording of The Underfall Yard, with Filkins being replaced by singer David Longdon. Dave Gregory (XTC), Jem Godfrey (Frost*) and Francis Dunnery (It Bites) make guest appearances on the album.

perplexity.description:
Welcome to the Planet is Big Big Train's fourteenth studio album, released in January 2022 through their English Electric Recordings label. The album arrived just six months after the band's critically acclaimed top 40 album Common Ground, with founder Gregory Spawton explaining that the pandemic's impact motivated the band to make swift use of their time and return to the studio with renewed energy from new band members. The nine-track collection showcases the band's characteristic blend of progressive rock with pastoral, emotionally resonant songwriting that draws from the sound worlds of early Genesis and Yes.

The album demonstrates both continuity and evolution within Big Big Train's established style. Tracks like "Made From Sunshine," "Lanterna," and "Oak and Stone" maintain the band's signature approach to intricate arrangements and lyrical depth, while the title track represents a notable departure—it marks Carly Bryant's debut songwriting contribution to the band, featuring music and lyrics entirely of her creation and standing as stylistically distinct from the band's previous work. The album balances shorter, focused pieces such as "Capitoline Venus" (2:27) with extended compositions like "Oak and Stone" (7:12), creating dynamic pacing across its runtime.

Welcome to the Planet received positive critical reception, with reviewers praising its cohesive quality and emotional impact. The album was not merely a collection of unreleased material from the Common Ground sessions but a fully realized work that critics felt enhanced their appreciation of the band's artistic range. It represents an important chapter in Big Big Train's discography, released during a transitional period for the band and showcasing their continued vitality within the progressive rock landscape.
